task.question: Let a degree-d polynomial be given by Bernstein coefficients c(0),...,c(d), all lying in a common interval [lo, hi]. Suppose we restrict the polynomial to a subinterval [u, v] with 0 <= u < v <= 1 by two successive de Casteljau subdivisions, producing new Bernstein coefficients c'(0),...,c'(d) for the restricted piece. Prove that every restricted coefficient c'(i) still lies in [lo, hi]. Identify the two structural facts about the Bernstein basis that make this true.

task.question: A reversible source-loader on three little-endian bits is defined by the rule that maps each slot value s in {0,...,7} to (s XOR 3) mod 8, i.e. it flips the two low-order bits of s. Prove that this loader is its own inverse (an involution) as a permutation of {0,...,7}, and give the explicit image list obtained by applying it to 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 in order. Explain why the involution property is exactly what lets the two bit-flip gates that realize it also undo it when applied a second time.
